learning: Record whether S-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall with the lower speed. If they stay at 1 with unchanged geometry, the loss is probably tied to the start pose or line_loss handling, and the next controller test should target those.
notes: Iteration 4 geometry held unchanged, with base_speed lowered from 1.3 to 1.2 to test whether bend entry speed causes the S-bend and slalom line losses. Gains and line-loss handling are kept fixed so the change is isolated.
rationale: Iteration 4 (mass 0.6 kg) scored 54.98, slightly below iteration 3 (55.27). Mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg changed max_error only from about 0.064 to 0.063 m, so mass is not a meaningful lever. The oval line loss stayed at 0 from the +/-0.05 m span, but the S-bend (0.95 events) and slalom (1.0 event) still lose the line on every trial. Those losses are on sharp bends, where the robot overshoots and the sum of readings drops below 0.05. Geometry is unchanged from iteration 4, as the Builder's intent and decision rules require, so the controller is the variable that changes. Iteration 0 at base_speed 1.8 gave the worst S-bend progress (0.04), and iteration 1 at 1.4 gave 0.165. That suggests entry speed into bends drives the overshoot. I therefore lower base_speed from 1.3 to 1.2 to give more correction time on the bends. I keep kp 2.5, kd 0.2 and ki 0.05, because kp 3.0 raised oscillation to 0.186 in iteration 1, and keep last_direction line-loss handling so the tested change is limited to speed. Expected result: if speed-into-bend is the cause, S-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0 and progress rises on those tracks. The score may still stay near 55 if the loss is caused by the start pose, which this package does not change. The cost is a slower run, so completion_time may rise.
